subject: Rogue subprocessor discovery — remediation & data transfer attestations
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@opalpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: OpalPay Compliance <compliance@opalpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T09:13:00-08:00
Subject: Unexpected telemetry vendor observed in production traces

Hi Marissa / Kimberly —

During our routine production security review this morning we noticed outbound calls to a domain owned by Tracklytics Inc. (tracklytics.io) originating from requests that pass through Redwood's hosted ingestion for our account. We do not see Tracklytics listed on the subprocessor roster in the DPA appendix you previously shared, and this was flagged by our security team as an unapproved telemetry recipient.

I've attached a small trace snippet showing the outbound host and a sample request header. Can you confirm whether Tracklytics is a Redwood subprocessor, or if this traffic could be coming from a dependency in our integration?

Attachments: trace-log-20261127.png (screenshot of traces)

We treat any vendor that receives request-level telemetry as in-scope for data protection — please advise urgently on next steps.

Thanks,
Elena Soto
Head of Trust & Safety
OpalPay
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@opalpay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected telemetry vendor observed in production traces

Hi Elena — thank you for the heads up and the trace. We're treating this as high priority.

Quick asks while we investigate:
- Can you confirm whether the sample includes any user identifiers (customer_id, email, phone) or just request/agent headers?
- Do you have a short list of endpoints/paths where the outbound calls appear?
- If possible, please share the full trace (redact PII) to the Drive link I created: https://drive.redwood.company/shared/opalpay-audit-20261127

Internal plan (we'll execute now):
1) Infra/security (Jonas) will pull flow logs and check whether the outbound connection is initiated by Redwood-hosted processes or embedded client-side SDKs.
2) Legal (Priyom) will assess DPA coverage and escalation steps if Tracklytics is not listed.
3) Ops (Kimberly) will prepare an ACL-based transient block for tracklytics.io if we confirm data egress.

We'll loop you in with updates within 4 business hours.

Marissa
Director, Customer Security & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: preliminary forensic findings re: tracklytics.io

Folks — quick update from infra forensic investigations. Summary attached (forensic-summary-20261128.pdf). Key points:
- Tracklytics connections originate from our public ingestion cluster handling OpalPay tenant streams; specifically from the request processing worker that forwards telemetry to downstream processors.
- The payloads include HTTP headers and occasionally device IP and a short session token when the client does not redact. We observed 6 sample requests that contained an 'x-customer-id' header (likely non-PII surrogate ids) and 2 that included an email-like string in a custom header (probable PII).
- Tracklytics appears to be an analytics SDK endpoint that OpalPay's client integration pulls in; however, the outbound call path traverses Redwood-hosted processing due to a transform step in OpalPay's ingestion config.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Apply a temporary egress ACL to block tracklytics.io for the OpalPay tenant while we sort DPA status. This will be reversible and we should schedule a short customer-impact window (5–10 minutes) to avoid breaking live flows.
2) Legal to request an attestation from OpalPay on why Tracklytics is included and whether they have a DPA with Tracklytics.
3) If Tracklytics will remain in the flow and receives PII, we must add them to Redwood's subprocessor roster and capture a DPA addendum + security questionnaire before re-enabling egress.

I'll stand by to run the ACL and help with a rollback plan.

Jonas
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@opalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, OpalPay Compliance <compliance@opalpay.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected telemetry vendor observed in production traces

Hi Elena — thanks for raising this and for the trace artifact. To move quickly we need the following from OpalPay:
- Formal confirmation whether Tracklytics is intentionally embedded in your client (yes/no) and the reason for inclusion.
- Whether Tracklytics processes any identifiers that would classify the data as personal data under our DPA (examples: email, phone, national id, un-hashed user ids).
- If Tracklytics is intentional, provide a copy of your contractual terms with Tracklytics or an attestation that you will execute a DPA addendum.

I'm attaching a DPA addendum template we can sign to add Tracklytics to Redwood's subprocessor roster while we obtain security evidence. Please review, sign, or propose edits. For speed, we also created a DocuSign envelope: https://na1.docusign.com/documents/XXYYZZ12345

If we do not receive the above within 48 hours, we will proceed with a temporary egress block to prevent potential PII leakage.

Attachment: dpa-addendum-template.docx

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Legal — Data Protection
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Action items — OpalPay / Tracklytics (remediation & notification)

Kimberly — finalizing the internal playbook before we notify OpalPay. Summary:
- Evidence: trace + forensic summary indicate occasional headers with what looks like email-like strings; treat as potential PII until OpalPay confirms.
- Immediate action taken: none yet. Priyom has requested a formal attestation and DPA addendum; DocuSign link is in his note. If we don't get confirmation in 48 hours we will enact the ACL block.
- If OpalPay confirms Tracklytics is intentional and will provide a DPA, prep the subprocessor addition notice (customer-facing) and our internal subprocessor registry update.

Please approve the draft notice in the Drive link and confirm you can deploy the transient ACL template for tenant 'opalpay-prod' (block tracklytics.io) on 2026-12-01 at 09:00 PT if required. If approved, I will send OpalPay the timeline and next steps tomorrow morning.

Quoted for context:
> On Nov 29, 2026, Priyom Das wrote:
> > If we do not receive the above within 48 hours, we will proceed with a temporary egress block to prevent potential PII leakage.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Security & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
